summary.headline: Arihant Superstructures Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 18.5% YoY to Rs 181 crore; FY26 EBITDA margin 23% and FY27 margin guided to 25-27%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated operating revenue was Rs 181 crore (up 18.5% YoY, up about 43% QoQ), with EBITDA of Rs 30 crore (up 37% YoY) and a 16.7% margin, which management attributed to the first-time recognition of World Villas costs including pre-operating and marketing expenses and higher interest. FY26 revenue was Rs 551 crore (up about 10.5%), EBITDA Rs 127 crore (up 21%) at 23% margin, and deliveries reached 1,721 units after OC for two Arihant Aspire Phase-I towers in Q4. Sales bookings for FY26 were Rs 977 crore on 1,155 units (12.58 lakh sq ft), with average realisation up 27% YoY to Rs 7,769 per sq ft. Management guided to over 2,000 deliveries and roughly Rs 700 crore revenue in FY27, and debt is expected to rise by about Rs 50 crore.

financial_highlights.change: PAT declined 15.9% YoY per analyst question

financial_highlights.value: 395 units; 3.98 lakh sq ft; Rs 313 crore
financial_highlights.change: Avg Rs 7,870 per sq ft, +5.5% YoY

financial_highlights.value: 1,155 units; 12.58 lakh sq ft; Rs 977 crore
financial_highlights.change: Booking value +10% YoY; avg Rs 7,769 per sq ft vs Rs 6,082 in FY25 (+27%)

financial_highlights.value: Gross debt Rs 873 crore; secured Rs 453 crore; unsecured Rs 361 crore
financial_highlights.change: Net debt to equity 1.81x as cited by analyst; interest cost Rs 677 million, up 65% per analyst

segments.name: Residential (Q4 FY26 deliveries)
segments.commentary: Two Arihant Aspire Phase-I towers received OC in Q4, delivering 657 units (about 7.37 lakh sq ft); FY26 deliveries totalled 1,721 units.

segments.name: World Villas / Town Villas (premium)
segments.commentary: Revenue recognition for World Villas began in Q4; 71 unsold units worth Rs 14 crore as of March 2026; about 112 villas under construction and Phase-I targeted for October 2027 completion, with overall project completion by 2030.

segments.name: Hospitality and annuity assets
segments.commentary: Five-star hotel in Panvel (inside World Villas) expected to start revenue in about 3-3.5 years; Khopoli four-star hotel (approx. Rs 60 crore) under approval, about 3 years; gymkhana about 800 memberships sold.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guided to 25-27%, with margins improving as the one-time World Villas pre-operating and marketing costs are behind it.
FY27 deliveries expected to exceed 2,000 units; key projects Arihant Aalishan (Kharghar Phase-II), Arihant Aspire Della Tower, Arihant Advika (Vashi), plus Arihant Anaika 5 and Arihant Aradhya in Q1.
FY27 revenue guided to around Rs 700 crore from Rs 500-550 crore, based on percentage-of-completion recognition.
FY27 pre-sales growth target of 25-30% CAGR.
FY27 construction capex of about Rs 400 crore across projects, including about Rs 75 crore for the gymkhana and hotel; total debt expected to rise by about Rs 50 crore.
Free cash flow expected to turn positive from FY27 or within about 2 years.
Cost inflation estimated at 3-5%, to be recovered through higher prices on unsold inventory.
World Villas Phase-II and Town Villas launch expected in FY27; new Arihant Aspire tower (Avanti at Shilphata) also planned.
capex_capacity: World Villas plus hospitality capex of about Rs 350 crore (per analyst's Rs 3.5 billion), funded through internal accruals and debt, with no equity raise planned for this project.
Arihant Aspire Phase-IV (Benita tower, 3.82 lakh sq ft saleable) capex about Rs 190 crore; launched in Q4 FY26.
Khopoli four-star hotel investment about Rs 60 crore, still in approval stage.
World Villas is approximately 23% complete with 55 of 180 Phase-I units sold, per the analyst's question.

Company gross development value (GDV) increased to about Rs 14,000 crore from about Rs 12,000-12,500 crore; land bank about 98 acres after adding about 20 acres in FY26 (about 78 acres at March 2025).
demand_pricing: World Villas price realisation increased by about Rs 1 crore per villa since launch; sector prices up on Navi Mumbai airport and infrastructure.
NRI enquiries and conversions for premium projects rose over the last two and a half months, per management.
Villa walk-ins improved, but the buying cycle is 75-120 days; World Villas velocity slowed as management prioritised margin over volume.
Transactions reported at pre-war levels, with some customers showing caution; management sees no stoppage in bookings.
Affordable segment still leads by transaction count, while mid-income and luxury mix rose in FY26, lifting realisations 27%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the World Villas Phase-I saleable area jump from 4.14 to 10 lakh sq ft with units rising only from 176 to 180?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most of the increase reflects converting RERA carpet area to saleable area for comparability, with some villa design changes adding carpet area; no new approvals were cited.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt reduction plan, and when will net debt/equity (1.81x) improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt is project-specific and repaid at completion; the Aspire Tata Capital loan fell from about Rs 82 crore (September) to Rs 40 crore (March) and will be fully repaid in FY27. Overall debt may rise by about Rs 50 crore.

qa_highlights.question: When does the company turn free-cash-flow positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects FCF positive from FY27, and certainly within about two years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of debt and repayment for unsecured loans?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended cost about 12.75%; secured about 12.5%, unsecured 13-13.5%. Unsecured promoter loans are repaid only after secured lenders.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 and FY28 delivery volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 deliveries are expected to exceed 2,000 units, with no project-wise FY28 guidance given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue stay around Rs 550 crore despite Rs 1,000 crore bookings, and what is the FY27 revenue path?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue follows percentage completion; management expects revenue of about Rs 700 crore in FY27 from Aalishan, Aspire Panvel and Advika deliveries.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex and debt plan?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 400 crore total construction capex in FY27, including about Rs 75 crore for the gymkhana and hotel; debt to rise about Rs 50 crore.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation of 3-5% from the geopolitical situation and rupee weakness; recovery depends on pricing the unsold inventory higher.
Interest cost up about 65% to Rs 677 million, with PAT down 15.9% YoY in FY26 and net debt/equity at 1.81x.
World Villas Phase-I velocity is slow (55 of 180 units sold); pricing discipline could keep sales pace weak.
Negative operating cash flow for four consecutive years; FCF positivity is targeted for FY27-FY28.
Delivery target of more than 2,000 units and Rs 700 crore revenue in FY27 require timely completions across several projects.
Macro sentiment risk linked to the PM's consumption appeal and NRI demand, which management says has not dented enquiries.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, deliveries and margin recovery, with the FY27 targets stated firmly. Evasive or vague on project-level delivery timing, pricing per unit, and gymkhana membership pricing, which it deferred to the sales team.
key_quotes: Key highlights during the quarter was that we achieved OC for two towers in Ar ihant Aspire Phase-I, wherein we delivered 657 units, which is approximately 7,37,000 square feet of area comprising both the towers.
So, we expect in this FY27 to increase our EBITDA margin and take it to 25%-27% range because the contribution from the new projects will add on to the P&L going further.
So, we are not seeking any specific fundraise for this project.
So, overall, debt could increase by another 50 crores from here.

adds.what: Arihant Aspire Phase-IV (Benita tower, 3.82 lakh sq ft saleable) residential tower, capex about Rs 190 crore
World Villas / Town Villas premium project, Phase-I (about 180 units, ~112 villas under construction), completion targeted October 2027
Khopoli four-star hotel (approx Rs 60 crore), still in approval stage, about 3 years

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue to about Rs 700 crore (from Rs 500-550 crore, ~27% growth at midpoint) and deliveries above 2,000 units, backed by named projects (Aalishan, Aspire Della, Advika, Anaika 5, Aradhya) and percentage-of-completion recognition, but no order-book or booking-backed numbers were quantified for the revenue step-up, and World Villas velocity slowed (4 villas sold in Q4).
